Acciona (ISIN ES0125220311) was trading at EUR 213.50 at Lang & Schwarz on October 9, 2026 at 12:08 p.m. CEST, up 1.33 percent versus EUR 210.70. As Investing.com reported on September 15, 2026, EQT and Norway's wealth fund had bid for Acciona Energia, keeping the strategic review central to the stock story.

Three milestones shaped first-half results

On July 2, 2026, Acciona completed the sale of a 64 MW Spanish hydropower portfolio, according to Yahoo Finance. On July 27, it completed the sale of a 361 MW wind portfolio for EUR 432 million, the same transcript states. On July 31, Acciona reported EUR 10,142 million in first-half revenue, up 10.00 percent year on year, while EBITDA fell 26.00 percent to EUR 1,153 million.

What does the backlog mean for cash flow?

The infrastructure division delivered EUR 384 million of EBITDA in the first half of 2026, up 12.00 percent year on year, while its construction, operations and maintenance backlog stood at EUR 22.4 billion. Concession backlog increased 40.00 percent to EUR 136 billion, according to Yahoo Finance. That mix gives the company a large contracted base, but the first-half figures also show the cost of asset-sale timing: attributable net profit was EUR 83 million, compared with pro forma profit of EUR 360 million after the July transactions.

Next reporting date is November 12

The next earnings date listed by Investing.com is November 12, 2026. The date gives the market a scheduled checkpoint for progress on asset rotation, debt reduction and the second-half contribution from infrastructure and energy.

Stock gains above prior close

Acciona stock was trading at EUR 213.50 at Lang & Schwarz on October 9, 2026 at 12:08 p.m. CEST, plus 1.33 percent versus the EUR 210.70 prior close. The 52-week range was EUR 165.00 to EUR 285.00 as of October 7, 2026, placing the reference price inside the established annual band. The further course of trading is shown by the continuously updated real-time quote of Acciona stock.
